Rashi on Shabbat 58a:11:1.hebrew: לא אידי ואידי דעבד ליה רביה - דאע"ג דכבול דמתניתין אוקימנא בדעבד איהו לנפשיה, התם הוא דאיכא לאוקמיה בסתם חותמות של טיט, דאי מיתבר — אין מקפיד עליו להביא שבריו לבית אדונו. הלכך, ליכא לאוקמיה בדעבד ליה רביה, דאי עבד ליה רביה לא הוה מיתסר, דכל זמן שלא נפסק לא שקיל ליה מצוארו משום אימתא דרביה, ואי מיפסק — לא קפיד עליה בעליו משום פסידא, דליכא פסידא; הלכך לא מייתי ליה. אבל הך, לא איכא לאוקמא בשל טיט, כדמסתברא לקמן מסיפא; הלכך, אפילו עבד ליה רביה נמי אסור, דאי מיפסק — קפיד עליה משום פסידא, ומירתת עבד ומייתי ליה בידיה:
Rashi on Shabbat 58a:11:1.english: No, both this and that are where his master made it for him - For even though we established the *kevol* of our Mishnah as [referring to a case] where he made it for himself, that is [only] there, where it can be established as standard clay seals, which if it breaks, [the master] is not particular about it [so as to require him] to bring its shards to his master's house. Therefore, it cannot be established [as a case] where his master made it for him, for had his master made it for him, it would not have been prohibited, since as long as it has not detached, he will not remove it from his neck out of fear of his master; and if it detaches, its owner is not particular about it on account of financial loss, since there is no financial loss; therefore, he will not bring it. But this [baraita] cannot be established as [referring to a seal] of clay, as is apparent below from the concluding clause; therefore, even if his master made it for him, it is also prohibited, for if it detaches, [the master] is particular about it on account of financial loss, and the slave will be afraid and will bring it in his hand.

Rashi on Shabbat 58a:11:2.hebrew: דבר המקפיד עליו רבו - אם יאבד: לא יצא — דאי מפסיק, מייתי ליה:
Rashi on Shabbat 58a:11:2.english: An object about which his master is particular - [Particular about it] if it gets lost: He may not go out [with it] — for if it snaps, he will bring it.

Rashi on Shabbat 58a:12:1.hebrew: מסתברא - דבשל מתכת קאי, מדאיצטריך למיתני "אין מקבלין טומאה". וטעמא — משום דלאו לנוי עבידא:
Rashi on Shabbat 58a:12:1.english: It is reasonable - That it refers to [a seal] of metal, since it was necessary to teach: "They cannot become ritually impure." And the reason is that it is not made for ornament.

Rashi on Shabbat 58a:12:2.hebrew: הני הוא דלא מקבלין טומאה - משום דלאו כלים נינהו, הא שאר כלי מתכות מקבלין:
Rashi on Shabbat 58a:12:2.english: These are the [objects] that do not contract ritual impurity - Because they are not [considered] vessels, but other metal vessels do contract [impurity].

Rashi on Shabbat 58a:13:1.hebrew: אלא אי אמרת - כלים דידהו — כלי העשוי מטיט כזה, שאינו מצרפו בכבשן מעשה ידי יוצר דניהוי קרוי כלי חרס, אלא כלי אדמה — מי מקבל טומאה?! בתמיה:
Rashi on Shabbat 58a:13:1.english: However, if you say - [Regarding the inference:] “Their vessels” — does a vessel made of such clay, which one does not fire in a kiln [through] the craft of a potter so that it would be called an earthenware vessel, but rather [remains merely] an earthen vessel, contract ritual impurity?! [This is asked] in astonishment.

Rashi on Shabbat 58a:14:1.english: Vessels of dung - Cattle dung from which one made a vessel.

Rashi on Shabbat 58a:17:1.hebrew: דמיחא מומחא - שארגו בבגד, ותו לא מיפסיק:
Rashi on Shabbat 58a:17:1.english: Where an expert wove it in - That he wove it into the garment, and it will no longer detach.

Rashi on Shabbat 58a:17:2.hebrew: לא גזרו - לצאת בו. ודרב הונא לענין אריג כי האי גוונא נמי איתמר, דאשמעינן דלא חיישינן תו לדלמא מיפסק:
Rashi on Shabbat 58a:17:2.english: They did not decree - Against going out with it. And [this statement] of Rav Huna was stated regarding an item woven in this manner as well, which teaches us that we are no longer concerned lest it tear off.

Rashi on Shabbat 58a:1:1.hebrew: אין בה משום עטרות כלות - דגזרו עליהן שלא תצא בהן מחורבן ואילך משום צער, במס' סוטה (דף מט.):
Rashi on Shabbat 58a:1:1.english: It is not subject to [the prohibition of] bridal crowns - For they decreed regarding them that [a bride] may not go out in them from the destruction [of the Temple] onward out of grief, in Tractate Sotah (daf 49a).

Rashi on Shabbat 58a:2:1.hebrew: ושמואל אמר - כבול דמתני' כבלא דעבדא, ופליג אדר' אבהו:
Rashi on Shabbat 58a:2:1.english: And Shmuel said - The kavul of the Mishnah is a slave’s chain, and he disagrees with Rabbi Abbahu.

Rashi on Shabbat 58a:2:2.hebrew: חותם שבצוארו - הוא כבלא דעבדא, והיו עושין אותו משל טיט:
Rashi on Shabbat 58a:2:2.english: A seal that is around his neck - This is the slave’s collar, and they used to make it of clay.

Rashi on Shabbat 58a:3:1.hebrew: דעביד ליה רביה - אית ליה אימתא, ולא שקיל ליה מצוארו להוליכו בידו. מיפסק החותם ונשבר — ומירתת מרבו, שלא יאמר שהוא נטלו להראות בשוק שהוא בן חורין:
Rashi on Shabbat 58a:3:1.english: Where his master made it for him - He has fear [of his master], and will not remove it from his neck to carry it in his hand. [If] the seal snaps and breaks, he is afraid of his master, lest [his master] say that he took it off to show in the marketplace that he is a free man.

Rashi on Shabbat 58a:5:1.hebrew: ומקפל ליה - הטלית על כתפיו, כדי שלא יראה מקום החותם ולא יבינו שנפל. ודמי הטלית על כתפו כמשוי:
Rashi on Shabbat 58a:5:1.english: And folds it - [He folds] the cloak onto his shoulders so that the place of the seal will not be seen, and they will not realize that it fell off. And the cloak on his shoulder is considered like a burden.

Rashi on Shabbat 58a:5:2.english: Is liable to bring a sin-offering - For it is not an adornment except when he wears it in the manner of a garment.

Rashi on Shabbat 58a:6:1.hebrew: כולהו רבנן לא ליפקו בסרבלי חתימי - היו עושין חותמות לטליתות שלהן כעין עבדים, להראות שהן כפופין לריש גלותא. לא ליפקו — דאי מפסקי, מרתתי ומקפלי להו:
Rashi on Shabbat 58a:6:1.english: All the Sages may not go out in sealed cloaks - They would make seals on their cloaks, like slaves, to show that they were subservient to the Exilarch. They may not go out [with them] — for if [the seals] break off, they will be afraid and fold them [and carry them on their shoulders].

Rashi on Shabbat 58a:6:2.english: Since they are not particular with regard to you - If you go without a seal.

Rashi on Shabbat 58a:7:1.hebrew: יוצא העבד בחותם שבצוארו - ובשל טיט, דלא קפיד עליה לאתויי. ואי משום דמירתת — מאי חורבא נפקא מינה? משום אימתא דרביה לא מייתי ליה בידיה, דהא לאו הוכחה היא דעבדות אלא כשישנו על צוארו או בכסותו:
Rashi on Shabbat 58a:7:1.english: A slave may go out with a seal that is around his neck - And [this refers to a seal made] of clay, where [the master] is not particular about it [for the slave] to bring it [back]. And if [one might suggest that] because he is afraid [of his master, he might carry it] — what mishap could result from this? Out of fear of his master he would not bring it in his hand, for this is not proof of servitude unless it is upon his neck or on his clothing.

Rashi on Shabbat 58a:8:1.hebrew: וזה וזה אין מקבלין טומאה - דלאו לנוי עביד שיהא טמא משום תכשיט. ואע"ג דבשל מתכת מוקמינן לה להא לקמן, מיהו לאו לנוי דיליה הוא אלא לגנאי, וכלי תשמיש נמי לא הוי:
Rashi on Shabbat 58a:8:1.english: And both this and that cannot become ritually impure - For it is not made for ornament, that it should be ritually impure as an ornament. And even though we establish this [baraita] later as [referring to a seal] of metal, nevertheless it is not for his adornment, but rather for [his] disgrace, and it is also not a utilitarian vessel.

Rashi on Shabbat 58a:8:2.english: Can become ritually impure - For it is an ornament.

Rashi on Shabbat 58a:8:3.english: A bell - It is made for ornament:

Rashi on Shabbat 58a:8:4.english: And not with a bell that is around his neck, but he may go out with a bell that is on his clothes - [The Gemara] explains the reason below.

Rashi on Shabbat 58a:9:1.english: That is on its garment - They make cloaks for horses so that they do not become soiled.

Rashi on Shabbat 58a:9:2.hebrew: לא תצא - כדאמרינן באידך פרקין (ד' נד:), דמתחזי כמאן דאזיל לחינגא:
Rashi on Shabbat 58a:9:2.english: [An animal] may not go out - As we say in our other chapter (54b), that it appears like one who is going to a celebration:

Rashi on Shabbat 58a:9:3.english: Cannot become ritually impure - For there is no [halakhic category of] ornament for an animal.

Tosafot on Shabbat 58a:16:1.hebrew: מאי שנא זוג שבצוארו דלמא מיפסיק ואתי לאתויי - והא דתנן לקמן (שבת דף סו:): "בני מלכים יוצאין בזוגין, וכל אדם — אלא שדברו חכמים בהווה"? אומר ר"י: דמיירי בזוגין יקרים שיוצאין בהן בני מלכים, כגון של כסף ושל זהב, דליכא למיחש בהו דילמא מיפסיק — דמסתמא תקועין הן יפה בשלשלאות של כסף. והכא מיירי בזוג דעלמא, דומיא דזוג של בהמה. ולמאי דמוקי לה בגמרא באריג בכסותו — אתי נמי שפיר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 58a:16:1.english: Why is a bell around his neck different? Lest it be severed and he come to carry it - And as for that which we learned later in a Mishnah (Shabbat 66b): "Princes may go out with bells, and [in fact] any person [may do so], but the Sages spoke in terms of the common practice"? Ri says that [the Mishnah] deals with precious bells with which princes go out, such as [bells] of silver and of gold, where there is no concern that it might be severed, because presumably they are well-fastened with chains of silver. And here it deals with an ordinary bell, similar to an animal's bell. And according to that which [the Gemara] establishes it in the Gemara as [referring to a bell that is] woven into his garment, it also works out well.

Tosafot on Shabbat 58a:17:1.hebrew: הב"ע דמחי - וא"ת: כי היכי דזוג איירי במחי, הכי נמי איירי חותם שבכסותו במחי, ואם כן, אמאי אסור? וי"ל: דזוג מותר לפי שדרך לאורגו בבגד, שאין שום בגד שלא יהא ראוי לנוי ותכשיט כזה, ולא הטריחוהו לפוסקו מכל בגדים ולגנות הבגד. אבל חותם — אין דרך לעשותו בכל הבגדים, שאינו יפוי הבגד; ולכך גזרו חכמים, אפילו בארוג בכסותו, שיהא צריך לפוסקו, אטו היכא שאין ארוג. וא"ת: אדמפליג בין זוג שבצוארו לזוג שבכסותו, ליפלוג בזוג שבכסותו גופיה בין מחי ללא מחי! ויש לומר: דניחא ליה לאשמעינן, דזוג שבצוארו אסור אפילו בחתיכת הבגד שסביב צוארו, ואינה יכולה ליפול אלא ע"י חתיכה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 58a:17:1.english: "Here we are dealing with [a case where] it is woven [into it]" - And if you say: Just as [the clause regarding] a bell deals with [where] it is woven [in], so too, [the clause regarding] a seal on his garment deals with [where] it is woven [in]; and if so, why is it forbidden? And it can be answered: A bell is permitted because it is standard practice to weave it into a garment, as there is no garment that is not suitable for such an ornament and adornment, and they did not trouble him to cut it out from all [his] garments and [thereby] disfigure the garment. But [with] a seal, it is not standard practice to make it on all garments, as it is not an embellishment of the garment; therefore, the Sages decreed, even [when it is] woven into his garment, that he must cut it out, [as a safeguard] due to [a case] where it is not woven [in]. And if you say: Rather than distinguishing between a bell around his neck and a bell on his garment, let it distinguish within [the case of] a bell on his garment itself, between [where it is] woven [in] and [where it is] not woven [in]! And it can be answered: It was preferable for it to teach us that a bell around his neck is forbidden even on a piece of cloth around his neck, where it cannot fall off except by means of cutting [the cloth].

Tosafot on Shabbat 58a:17:2.hebrew: כדרב הונא כו' - ואע"ג דמילתא דרב הונא אייתי לעיל (שבת דף נז.) גבי חציצה, מדקאמר "כל שהוא אריג" משמע דה"ק: בין לענין חציצה, בין לענין דלמא מיפסיק — לא חיישינן באריג:
Tosafot on Shabbat 58a:17:2.english: In accordance with Rav Huna, etc. - And even though Rav Huna's statement was cited above (Shabbat 57a) regarding interposition, since he said, "Anything that is woven," it implies that this is what he means: whether regarding interposition or regarding [the concern that] perhaps it will tear off, we are not concerned with [an item that is] woven.

Tosafot on Shabbat 58a:2:1.hebrew: והאמר שמואל יוצא העבד בחותם כו' - ולא בעי לאוקמי מתניתין בחותם שבכסותו, דניחא ליה לאוקמה בדעבד איהו לנפשיה, ואיירי מתני' בכל חותמות:
Tosafot on Shabbat 58a:2:1.english: And didn't Shmuel say: A slave may go out with a seal, etc. - And [the Gemara] did not want to establish the Mishnah as [referring to] a seal on his clothes, because it preferred to establish it as [a case where] he made it for himself, so that the Mishnah is dealing with all seals.

Tosafot on Shabbat 58a:3:1.hebrew: הא דעבד איהו לנפשיה - קשה לרשב"א: אמאי שריא מתני' בדעבד איהו לנפשיה בחצר, כיון דליכא קפידא דרבו? וי"ל, דאיכא קצת קפידא, אבל לא כל כך כמו בעבד ליה רביה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 58a:3:1.english: That [case where] he made it for himself - The Rashba finds it difficult: Why does the Mishnah permit [going out] in a courtyard in [a case where] he made it for himself, since there is no strictness from his master? And it can be answered that there is a slight strictness, but not as much as when his master made it for him.

Tosafot on Shabbat 58a:4:1.hebrew: במאי אוקימתא להא דשמואל בדעבד ליה רביה כו' - אבל אי מיירי בדעבד איהו לנפשיה, אתי שפיר: דבצוארו ליכא למיחש דלמא פסיק ליה בידים כדי שלא יבינו הרואין שהוא עבד, אבל בכסותו איכא למיחש דלמא מקפל טליתו לכסות החותם, ולא ידע דיש בזה חיוב חטאת. אבל בדעבד ליה רביה — משום אימתא דרביה ירא לקפל. והשתא נמי ידע הש"ס לדרב יצחק, אלא דלא ידע שיש לחוש דילמא מיפסיק; ובתר דמשני, מייתי דרב יצחק, ונחת לפרושי שיש חיוב חטאת בקיפול:
Tosafot on Shabbat 58a:4:1.english: In what case did you establish this statement of Shmuel? Where his master made it for him, etc. - But if it were dealing with [a case where] he made it for himself, it would work out well: for with [a seal] around his neck, there is no concern that perhaps he will sever it by hand so that onlookers will not realize that he is a slave; whereas with [a seal] on his clothing, there is concern that perhaps he will fold his cloak to conceal the seal, not knowing that there is liability for a sin-offering in this. However, where his master made it for him, out of dread of his master he would be afraid to fold [his cloak]. And at this point as well, the Talmud knew of [the ruling of] Rav Yitzchak, but it did not know that there is concern lest it sever [on its own]; and after it answers, it cites [the statement of] Rav Yitzchak and proceeds to explain that there is liability for a sin-offering in folding.

Tosafot on Shabbat 58a:5:1.hebrew: דילמא מיפסק ומרתת ומקפל ליה - דניחא ליה טפי שיהיה מקופל, משיראה רבו שנפסק לגמרי, ויסבור שבמזיד פסקו למרוד בו:
Tosafot on Shabbat 58a:5:1.english: "Perhaps it will be severed, and he will fear and fold it" - For it is preferable to him that [the garment] be folded, rather than that his master should see that it was completely severed and assume that he intentionally severed it to rebel against him.

Tosafot on Shabbat 58a:9:1.hebrew: לא תצא בהמה כו' - דמיחזי כמאן דאזיל לחינגא, כדפי' בקונ'. דלא מצינן למימר משום דילמא מיפסיק ואתי לאתויי — דהא לעיל (דף נד:) מפרש דזוג אסור משום דמיחזי כמאן דאזיל לחינגא, ולא קאמר "דלמא מיפסק" דומיא דחותם:
Tosafot on Shabbat 58a:9:1.english: "An animal may not go out, etc." - [It is forbidden] because it looks like one who is going to a market, as explained in the Kuntres. For we cannot say [that it is forbidden] because [of the concern that] it might snap and he will come to carry it, as earlier (54b) [the Gemara] explains that a bell is forbidden because it looks like one who is going to a market, and it did not say "lest it snap", as [it does] in the case of a seal.
